objective: From official SQLite documentation, compare rollback DELETE journaling with WAL for concurrent readers and writers, simultaneous writers, and use across a network filesystem. Answer in French with read citations and qualifications.

sources.title: Write-Ahead Logging
sources.snippet: There are advantages and disadvantages to using WAL instead of a rollback journal. Advantages include: WAL is significantly faster in most scenarios. WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers.
sources.discovered_by: site:sqlite.org WAL rollback journal DELETE concurrent readers writers network filesystem

sources.title: File Locking And Concurrency In SQLite Version 3
sources.snippet: The document only describes locking for the older rollback-mode transaction mechanism. Locking for the newer write-ahead log or WAL mode is described separately. SQLite Version 3.0.0 introduced a new locking and journaling mechanism designed to improve concurrency over SQLite version 2 and to reduce the writer starvation problem.

sources.title: SQLite User Forum: Using WAL mode with multiple processes
sources.snippet: WAL journal mode supports one writer and many readers at the same time. A second writer will have to wait until the first write transaction is committed or rolled back.

sources.title: SQLite User Forum: Exclusive write-only lock? (Allow only one process read-write, and multiple read-only)
sources.snippet: Note that these are two very different things. In the normal journaling modes, SQLite will "wait" for writers to finish transactions before readers can read. Only in WAL mode can you have readers reading existing data WHILE a writer is writing new data.
